title: Two Streets, Two Degrees: How Cities Are Finding Room to Grow Green
title_zh: 两条街，两度温差：城市如何在缝隙里种出绿色
intro_zh: 本文约 545 词，语言难度接近四级阅读真题，含 6 个四级核心词汇（concrete、shade、absorb、narrow、benefit、maintain）。文章以麦德林、首尔、新加坡、米兰的具体做法和数据为例，说明城市绿色空间的作用、落地方式与维护成本，适合练习细节定位与推理判断。

paragraphs.en: On a hot afternoon in Medellín, Colombia, two streets can feel like two different cities. One is bare concrete, bright with heat. The other, only thirty metres away, is lined with trees, bamboo and flowering bushes. In 2019 the city planted thousands of plants along its roads and slopes. Local planners call the lines of green 'corridors', and researchers later found that some streets had become about two degrees cooler.
paragraphs.zh: 在哥伦比亚的麦德林，一个炎热的下午，两条街能让人感觉像两座不同的城市。一条是裸露的混凝土，被晒得发亮。另一条相距不过三十米，两旁种着树木、竹子和开花的灌木。2019 年，这座城市在道路和坡地上种下了成千上万株植物。当地规划者把这些绿色带状区域称为“廊道”，研究者后来发现，一些街道的温度下降了约两度。

paragraphs.en: A city is mostly made of hard surfaces. Concrete, asphalt and glass soak up sunlight all day and give it back slowly at night, which is why a city centre can be five degrees warmer than the countryside around it. Green space works against this. Leaves use sunlight to make food instead of turning it into heat, and they hold water that cools the air as it evaporates. On a street with old trees, the pavement beneath them can be ten degrees cooler than the open road, and that shade changes how people use the street.
paragraphs.zh: 城市主要由坚硬的地面构成。混凝土、沥青和玻璃整天吸收阳光，夜里再慢慢释放出来，这就是市中心会比周边乡村高出五度的原因。绿色空间正好与之相抗。树叶用阳光制造养分，而不是把它变成热；叶片还储存水分，水蒸发时让空气变凉。在有大树的街上，树下的人行道可能比没有遮拦的路面低十度，而这片阴凉改变了人们使用街道的方式。

paragraphs.en: Plants also deal with rain. When a storm hits a city that is covered in concrete, water has nowhere to go. It rushes into drains, and the drains overflow. Parks, gardens and even narrow strips of grass beside a road absorb water like a sponge, holding it until it can sink slowly into the ground. Several older cities are now pulling up concrete and putting in small gardens for exactly this reason.
paragraphs.zh: 植物还要应对雨水。当暴雨袭击一座被混凝土覆盖的城市时，水无处可去，只能冲进下水道，而下水道会溢出。公园、花园，甚至路边窄窄的草带，都能像海绵一样吸水，把水留住，让水慢慢渗入地下。如今有几座老城正因此撬开混凝土，改建成小花园。

paragraphs.en: Then comes the question of room. Land in a city is expensive, and many neighbourhoods have no empty space at all. So some cities look up. Singapore requires new buildings to give back the garden they cover, by placing plants on roofs and walls. Milan's Bosco Verticale carries around 900 trees on two tower blocks, and the building stays cooler in summer because of them.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来是空间问题。城市土地昂贵，许多街区根本没有空地。于是有些城市开始向上看。新加坡要求新建筑把占掉的花园还回来，办法是在屋顶和墙面上种植物。米兰的“垂直森林”在两栋高楼上种了约九百棵树，因为这些树，大楼在夏天更凉快。

paragraphs.en: Others look at what is already there. Seoul removed a highway in 2003 and restored the stream that ran beneath it. The Cheonggyecheon is now a 5.8-kilometre park in the middle of the city, visited by tens of thousands of people every day, and the air around it is cooler than in neighbouring districts.
paragraphs.zh: 另一些城市则着眼于已有之物。首尔在 2003 年拆掉了一条高架路，修复了它下面的河道。清溪川如今是市中心一座长 5.8 公里的公园，每天有数万人到访，周边的空气也比相邻城区凉爽。

paragraphs.en: The benefit is not only about temperature. Doctors in several countries now write 'park prescriptions': a walk among trees lowers stress and helps people sleep. Children who can reach a park without crossing a busy road play outside far more often. Shop owners on green streets often notice that more people stop, walk and spend. A well-used park is a public service, not just decoration.
paragraphs.zh: 好处不只在温度上。好几个国家的医生现在会开“公园处方”：在树林中散步能减压、助眠。不必横穿车流就能到达公园的孩子，在户外玩耍的次数明显更多。绿树成荫的街道上，店主常会发现更多人停下来、走一走、花点钱。一个被充分使用的公园是一项公共服务，不只是装饰。

paragraphs.en: None of this happens by itself. A park needs water, workers and money to maintain. A young tree may need watering for two summers before its roots reach deep, cool soil. Cities that set aside a small budget for care every year do far better than those that open a beautiful park once and then forget it. Care is the quiet half of the work.
paragraphs.zh: 这一切都不会自动发生。一座公园需要水、人力和资金来维护。一棵小树可能要浇上两个夏天的水，根才能扎进深层凉爽的土壤里。每年留出一笔小小的养护预算的城市，远比那些风风光光建好一座漂亮公园、随后就不管了的城市做得好。养护是这项工作中安静的那一半。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the most useful lesson is that green space does not have to be a large park. A row of trees, a narrow strip of grass, a garden on a roof — each does a little. Spread them across a city, and the effect adds up. The green city is not built in one project; it is built street by street.
paragraphs.zh: 也许最有用的启示是：绿色空间不必是一座大公园。一排树、一条窄草带、屋顶上的一块花园——每一个都起一点作用。把它们散布到整座城市，效果就会叠加。绿色城市不是靠一个工程建成的，而是一条街一条街地建成的。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Trees in cities are grown mainly to make streets look pretty.
Cities are finding creative ways to add green space, and that space brings real benefits.
Rooftop gardens are always cheaper than traditional parks.
Drivers should give up their cars in city centres.
questions.explain: 全文以麦德林、首尔、新加坡、米兰为例，说明城市如何在有限空间里增加绿地（道路绿化、屋顶墙面、修复河道），并指出绿地在降温、蓄水、健康和经济方面的实际好处，因此 B 概括最全面。A、C 过于片面，D 文中未提。

questions.q: According to the passage, what did Medellín do in 2019?
options: It removed a highway and restored a stream.
It required new buildings to put plants on roofs and walls.
It planted thousands of plants along its roads and slopes.
It built a 5.8-kilometre park in the city centre.
questions.explain: 第一段明确写道 In 2019 the city planted thousands of plants along its roads and slopes，故答案为 C。A 和 D 是首尔清溪川的做法，B 是新加坡的规定，属于典型的细节张冠李戴。

questions.q: What can be inferred from the last two paragraphs?
options: A park is finished once it is built and opened to the public.
Long-term care costs as much attention as the first construction.
Only very large parks can make a city cooler.
Young trees need no water after they are planted.
questions.explain: 倒数第二段说每年留出养护预算的城市远好于建完就忘的城市，最后一段又强调绿地不必很大、关键是“一条街一条街”地积累，可推知后期养护与最初建设同等重要，故选 B。A、D 与原文相反，C 与最后一段“不必是大公园”矛盾。

questions.q: The word 'corridors' in Paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: narrow strips that link one place to another
groups of workers who plant trees
questions.explain: 此处 corridors 指麦德林沿道路和坡地种出的“绿色带状区域”，把不同地点连接起来，与 B“连接两地的狭长地带”最接近。原文说 these lines of green，说明是可看见的带状绿化，而不是地下隧道、室内房间或工人群体。
